description:
From the fz-kdt.106 cold review (2026-09-01). ACTIVATION_INPUT_ROW_BUDGET
firing is the primary signal that the compiler is doing history-driven
rather than input-driven work, and after fz-kdt.106 lands a fire means
GENUINE correlation width. The fz-kdt.106 build (eace470ea) landed a
REAL public telemetry event for it (allowlisted, readable from
--log-telemetry) but via a THREAD-LOCAL ledger drained in drive.rs --
JoinContribution::Ctx is an associated type, so a borrowed sink cannot
ride the context without a GAT on all three implementors, and World
holds no telemetry handle. THIS TICKET'S REMAINING WORK: decide whether
the thread-local producer/drain split (which follows the existing
flush_reported_warnings precedent) is the permanent shape or whether a
first-class threaded sink is worth the GAT plumbing; if the former,
close with that decision recorded. The event feeds fz-zih's
collapse-cascade work-ratchet fixture. Baseline at 1d44ac7cd: 3 of 449
dumping fixtures collapse at base (00420 at 30,
behavior/enum_take_drop_split at 30, behavior/enum_predicate_search at
28; 88 events corpus-wide); zero after dominance absorption (the
engineered stress shape still collapses 3x -- genuine correlation width,
by design).
title: The activation-input row budget needs a telemetry event: a collapse is the history-vs-input work signal
